summary.headline: Nuvoco Q1 FY27: volume up 5% YoY to 5.3 mt and EBITDA up 7% to INR572 crore, highest-ever Q1 for both.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 volume rose 5% YoY to 5.3 million tons and EBITDA rose 7% YoY to INR572 crore, the company's highest-ever first-quarter volume and EBITDA. Realisation rose about INR320 per ton QoQ, largely offset by about INR230 per ton of cost inflation (power and fuel, raw material, packing bags, freight, fixed-cost deleverage), leaving a net EBITDA gain of about INR90 per ton. Management said the Surat grinding unit (2 mtpa) was inaugurated on 11 July 2026, ahead of schedule, and Kutch clinker and grinding remain on track for phased start from Q3 FY27. Management guided Q2 cost increase of about INR100 per ton, with power and fuel up INR30-40 per ton and packing and freight easing.

financial_highlights.value: Up about INR320 per ton QoQ (Q1 vs Q4)
financial_highlights.change: Cost inflation about INR230 per ton; net EBITDA impact about INR90 per ton
vs INR5,274 crore a year earlier (about INR600 crore lower)
FY27 capex guidance INR900 crore unchanged

segments.name: North (Chittorgarh, Nimbol, Rajasthan)
segments.commentary: Petcoke share cut from over 50% to about 40% by moving open-market coal from Chhattisgarh and Varanasi; Rajasthan capacity to be freed up for the North as Surat comes online.

segments.name: East (Risda, Sonadih, Arasmeta, Jojobera, Panagarh, Jajpur)
segments.commentary: Risda petcoke share cut from about 37% to about 25% and Arasmeta at zero petcoke, using Sonepur Bazari coal and sweetener. Jojobera and Panagarh CTOs are nearly done; Jajpur awaits NIPL certificate; Arasmeta targeted for end FY27.

segments.name: Gujarat / West (Surat, Kutch, Sachana)
segments.commentary: Surat 2 mtpa grinding inaugurated 11 July 2026; sales in Gujarat currently about 1.3-1.4 mt, targeted near 2 mtpa annualised by Q4 FY27. Kutch clinker and grinding phased from Q3 FY27; Sachana bulk terminal targeted Q2 FY28.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 total cost expected to rise about INR100 per ton QoQ (give or take INR20-30); power and fuel up INR30-40 per ton due to kiln and mill shutdowns, with packing bag costs seen cooling INR20-25 per ton and freight easing with the lean-season discount from 1 August.
Fuel cost expected to stay broadly flat in Q2 (1.52 could move to 1.55); petcoke inventory adequate for the quarter at similar cost; Q3 may carry higher-cost inventory.
FY27 volume growth target of about 7-8%, in line with market demand expectations of 7-8% over the next three quarters.
FY27 capex INR900 crore unchanged; FY28 capex INR950-1,000 crore including Vadraj expansion, Sachana terminal and routine capex.
Gujarat EBITDA per ton expected to be below company average in year 1 and to match rest-of-North in years 2-3; no EBITDA-per-ton guidance given.
Kutch clinker earliest start about January 2027 with Kutch clinker supply to Surat from start of FY28; East capacity (Jojobera, Panagarh, Jajpur, Arasmeta) to be ready by end FY27 for FY28 volumes.
capex_capacity: Surat grinding unit: 2 mtpa inaugurated 11 July 2026, ahead of schedule; first Western region capacity addition and frees Rajasthan capacity for the North.
Kutch clinker unit: major equipment delivered; kiln rotation complete; overhaul and trial preparation within Q2 FY27; phased operations from Q3 FY27.
Kutch grinding unit: civil works targeted for completion by Q2 FY27; Kutch railway siding ballast and sleeper laying in progress.
Sachana bulk cement terminal with dedicated railway siding: work commenced, targeted operational by Q2 FY28.
East: plan to add 4 mtpa in phases till FY28; Jojobera and Panagarh about 1 mt each of headroom, targeted to lift dispatch to about 20,000 tons/day and 8,500 tons/day respectively in Q4.
demand_pricing: Management says market demand grew about 7-7.5% in Q1 and expects 7-8% over the next three quarters; Central government capex up 13% YoY to INR2.5 lakh crore quarter-to-date to May 2026.

Q1 realisation up about INR320 per ton QoQ: trade price up about INR10 per bag and non-trade about INR15-20 per bag in East; North up about INR10 trade and INR10-13 non-trade; price rise late March and geo-mix contributed.
No price drop in the first 14 days of July 2026; company has not taken a further price increase but will raise prices if costs fall.
Premium share at 42% in Q1 (peak 44% in Q4); Concreto about 4 mt, Duraguard Microfiber and Concreto Uno each about 1 mt annualised.
Management expects pricing to stay stable given limited clinker capacity additions over the next three years and capacity utilisation in East expected to return above 80% within 18-24 months.
Management said it lost about 0.2 mt of sales in April-June due to rake shortages, diesel shortages and truck shortages.

qa_highlights.question: Given Surat is online, what volume is expected this year and what is the clinker source before Kutch starts?
qa_highlights.answer: Gujarat sales of about 1.3-1.4 mt now; target about 2 mtpa annualised by Q4 FY27. Clinker for the incremental volume comes from the Chhattisgarh cluster and bartering; Kutch clinker expected to supply Surat from start of FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of East debottlenecking (CTOs for Jojobera, Panagarh, Jajpur, Arasmeta)?
qa_highlights.answer: Jojobera and Panagarh CTOs almost done; Jajpur awaits NIPL certificate; Arasmeta technical design done and ball mill procurement underway. All four to be ready by end FY27 and needed for FY28; no delay per management.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 realisation gain was price versus trade mix and geo-mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Three drivers: price increases (biggest), premium mix with Concreto, Duraguard Microfiber and Uno (about 5 mt premium and super-premium), and geo-mix shift toward high-realisation states (Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Rajasthan, Western MP). Trade mix unchanged at 75%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost outlook for Q2 and fuel and packing trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Total cost up about INR100 per ton QoQ (plus or minus INR20-30). Petcoke inventory covers Q2 at similar cost; packing bags to ease INR20-25 per ton; rake availability improving to about 4 per day; power and fuel up INR30-40 per ton from shutdowns.

qa_highlights.question: Will Gujarat (Surat and Kutch) EBITDA per ton converge with the company average, and how fast?
qa_highlights.answer: Year 1 EBITDA per ton will be lower due to high costs and aggressive volume push, with no dilution of price intended; modelling shows Gujarat EBITDA per ton equal to rest-of-North in years 2-3. Kutch, Sachana and Surat form a hub-and-spoke network.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any change to FY27 capex and what is the FY28 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex unchanged at INR900 crore with about INR370 crore spent in Q1; FY28 capex INR950-1,000 crore including Vadraj, Sachana terminal and routine spend.

risks_watch: Fuel and freight volatility: petcoke spiked to INR2.56 per million kcal; company booked at 2.05-2.15; Q3 may carry higher-cost inventory.
Rail and truck logistics: rake shortages (3.2-3.3 per day in Q1 vs 4 per day now) and diesel and truck shortages cost volume and freight; monsoon may restrict coal and clinker movement.
Gujarat ramp: Year-1 EBITDA per ton below company average; pricing discipline under aggressive volume push.
Kutch and Surat timelines: Kutch clinker start earliest around January 2027; Kutch grinding civil works to finish Q2 FY27; Sachana terminal Q2 FY28.
East pricing and capacity: management expects East utilisation to rise above 80% in 18-24 months; West Asia geopolitics unresolved.
Premium share fell from 44% to 42% QoQ; watch whether it recovers.
summary.management_tone: Confident on execution and cost control, with Surat inaugurated early and Q2 cost outlook given specific numbers; cautious on geopolitics and fuel. Management was evasive on EBITDA per ton guidance, declining to give a figure beyond stating that pricing should be stable.
key_quotes: We have had a strong start to the year, delivering higher business performance.
This represents a defining milestone in the history of the company, signifying our first-ever capacity expansion in the Western region.
I'm fairly confident that we will not dilute prices to push volumes in Gujarat.
Net-net, realization happened INR320 and the cost increase was close to about INR230, which reflects in the EBITDA impact of close to INR90.
